questions.text:
Answer ALL four parts. Each part carries 5 marks.

(a) Rectification of Errors: The Trial Balance of Vishnu Traders as on 31st March, 2025 did not agree and the difference was placed in a Suspense Account. The Profit disclosed by the draft Profit & Loss Account was Rs. 1,85,000. Subsequently the following errors were detected:
(i) Sales Day Book for March was overcast by Rs. 6,000.
(ii) A credit purchase of goods from Ravi for Rs. 12,400 was recorded in the Purchases Day Book as Rs. 14,200; Ravi's account was credited with the correct amount.
(iii) Repairs to machinery Rs. 9,000 were debited to Machinery Account. Depreciation is charged at 10% p.a. on machinery on closing balance; the repairs were carried out on 1st April 2024.
(iv) Goods costing Rs. 5,000 taken by the proprietor for personal use were not recorded at all.
(v) A cheque of Rs. 7,500 received from Sunil, a debtor, was correctly entered in the Cash Book but was posted to the debit of Sunil's account.
Pass rectifying journal entries, prepare the Suspense Account, and compute the corrected net profit.

(b) Bank Reconciliation Statement: On 31st March 2025 the Cash Book of Meera Enterprises showed a bank overdraft of Rs. 42,600. On comparison with the pass book the following were found: (i) Cheques issued for Rs. 68,000 of which cheques worth Rs. 23,500 were presented before 31st March. (ii) Cheques deposited Rs. 55,000, out of which Rs. 18,200 were credited by the bank on 3rd April. (iii) Bank charges Rs. 850 and interest on overdraft Rs. 2,340 debited by the bank not recorded in the Cash Book. (iv) A customer directly deposited Rs. 14,000 in the bank, no entry in Cash Book. (v) A cheque of Rs. 4,600 deposited and credited by bank was recorded in the Cash Book as Rs. 6,400. (vi) The bank wrongly debited the account with Rs. 3,000 belonging to another customer. Prepare a Bank Reconciliation Statement and ascertain the balance as per Pass Book.

(c) Accounting Standards / Concepts: (i) State and briefly explain any four fundamental accounting assumptions/qualitative characteristics relevant to preparation of financial statements. (ii) Anand Ltd. values its closing inventory of 2,000 units at cost Rs. 120 per unit. Due to a fall in demand the net realisable value is Rs. 104 per unit; however selling expenses of Rs. 6 per unit are still to be incurred and are included in arriving at NRV. State with reason the value at which closing inventory should be shown as per AS 2 and the amount of write-down.

(d) Depreciation: Kalyani Mills purchased a machine on 1st July 2021 for Rs. 8,00,000 and incurred Rs. 40,000 on installation. On 1st October 2023 an additional machine costing Rs. 3,00,000 was purchased. On 1st January 2025 the machine purchased on 1st July 2021 was sold for Rs. 4,20,000. Depreciation is provided at 15% p.a. on the written down value basis and the books are closed on 31st March each year. Prepare the Machinery Account for the years ended 31st March 2022 to 31st March 2025 (four years), showing profit or loss on sale.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 5 marks — Journal entries 3, Suspense A/c 1, corrected profit 1.
(i) Sales A/c Dr 6,000 to Suspense 6,000 (profit -6,000). (ii) Suspense Dr 1,800 to Purchases 1,800 (profit +1,800). (iii) Repairs A/c Dr 9,000 to Machinery 9,000; excess depreciation for FY 2024-25 = 10% of 9,000 = 900 written back: Machinery/Provision Dr 900 to Depreciation 900. Net effect on profit = -9,000 + 900 = -8,100. (iv) Drawings A/c Dr 5,000 to Purchases (or Trading) 5,000 → profit +5,000. (v) Suspense Dr 15,000 to Sunil 15,000 (posting to debit instead of credit; double error 2 × 7,500) — no profit effect.
Suspense A/c: Credit 6,000 (i); Debits 1,800 (ii) + 15,000 (v) = 16,800; opening difference (debit balance carried in trial balance) = 16,800 - 6,000 = 10,800 credit side opening i.e. Suspense had a credit opening balance of Rs. 10,800.
Corrected profit = 1,85,000 - 6,000 + 1,800 - 8,100 + 5,000 = Rs. 1,77,700.
(b) 5 marks. Start with overdraft as per Cash Book (42,600) — treat as negative. Add (increase overdraft): unpresented cheques reduce overdraft → cheques issued but not presented 68,000 - 23,500 = 44,500 (deduct from overdraft); cheques deposited not credited 18,200 (add to overdraft); bank charges 850 + interest 2,340 (add); direct deposit by customer 14,000 (deduct); cheque recorded 6,400 instead of 4,600 → Cash Book overstated deposit by 1,800 (add to overdraft); wrong debit by bank 3,000 (add). Computation: 42,600 - 44,500 + 18,200 + 850 + 2,340 - 14,000 + 1,800 + 3,000 = Rs. 10,290 overdraft as per Pass Book. Award 3 for correct treatment of items, 2 for final figure Rs. 10,290 (Dr. balance/overdraft as per Pass Book).
(c) 5 marks. (i) 2.5 marks — Going concern, consistency, accrual (fundamental assumptions per AS 1) plus qualitative characteristics: understandability, relevance, reliability, comparability; one line each. (ii) 2.5 marks — AS 2 requires inventory at lower of cost and net realisable value. NRV given is Rs. 104 (already net of selling expenses of Rs. 6, i.e. estimated selling price Rs. 110 less Rs. 6). Since NRV Rs. 104 < cost Rs. 120, value inventory at 2,000 × 104 = Rs. 2,08,000; write-down = 2,000 × 16 = Rs. 32,000 charged to P&L in the period of write-down.
(d) 5 marks. Machine I cost = 8,00,000 + 40,000 = 8,40,000 (capitalise installation).
FY 2021-22 (1.7.21 to 31.3.22, 9 months): dep = 8,40,000 × 15% × 9/12 = 94,500; WDV = 7,45,500.
FY 2022-23: dep = 1,11,825; WDV = 6,33,675.
FY 2023-24: Machine I dep = 95,051 (6,33,675 × 15%), WDV = 5,38,624; Machine II 3,00,000 from 1.10.23, dep 6 months = 22,500, WDV = 2,77,500.
FY 2024-25: Machine I dep 1.4.24 to 1.1.25 (9 months) = 5,38,624 × 15% × 9/12 = 60,595; WDV at sale = 4,78,029; sold for 4,20,000 → Loss on sale = Rs. 58,029. Machine II dep = 2,77,500 × 15% = 41,625; closing WDV = 2,35,875.
Marks: correct capitalisation 0.5, yearly depreciation 2.5, loss on sale 1, ledger format/balances 1. Minor rounding differences acceptable.

verification.method: Each part solved independently and re-computed; arithmetic cross-checked by recomputation of totals and balances
checks: Rectification: profit effect items re-added (185000-6000+1800-8100+5000 = 177700)
Suspense A/c debits 16,800 vs credits 6,000 gives opening credit balance 10,800 — internally consistent
BRS: item-wise direction verified from overdraft starting point; final overdraft 10,290 recomputed
AS 2 rule 'lower of cost or NRV' applied; NRV stated net of selling costs to avoid double deduction
Depreciation WDV chain recomputed year by year; loss on sale = 4,78,029 - 4,20,000 = 58,029

questions.text:
(a) (12 marks) From the following Trial Balance of M/s Deepak & Sons as on 31st March 2025, prepare the Trading and Profit & Loss Account for the year ended on that date and a Balance Sheet as at that date.
Debit balances: Opening Stock 1,20,000; Purchases 8,60,000; Wages 1,45,000; Carriage Inward 18,000; Salaries 1,32,000; Rent & Taxes 66,000; Advertisement 40,000; Bad Debts 9,000; Sundry Debtors 3,60,000; Cash at Bank 84,000; Cash in Hand 12,000; Furniture 1,50,000; Plant & Machinery 5,00,000; Insurance 24,000; Drawings 60,000; Carriage Outward 15,000. Total 25,95,000.
Credit balances: Capital 7,00,000; Sales 15,40,000; Sundry Creditors 2,68,000; Bills Payable 45,000; Provision for Doubtful Debts 12,000; Discount Received 8,000; Bank Loan (taken 1.10.2024 @ 12% p.a.) 2,00,000; Purchase Returns 22,000. Total 25,95,000.
Adjustments:
(i) Closing Stock: cost Rs. 1,95,000, net realisable value Rs. 1,88,000.
(ii) Depreciate Plant & Machinery @ 10% p.a. and Furniture @ 15% p.a.
(iii) Write off further bad debts Rs. 10,000 and maintain Provision for Doubtful Debts at 5% on debtors.
(iv) Insurance includes Rs. 6,000 paid for the year ending 30th June 2025.
(v) Outstanding wages Rs. 11,000 and outstanding salaries Rs. 8,000.
(vi) Interest on bank loan has not been paid for the year.
(vii) Goods costing Rs. 14,000 were distributed as free samples; no entry passed.

(b) (8 marks) Explain the difference between Capital Expenditure and Revenue Expenditure. Classify the following, giving one-line reasons:
(1) Rs. 55,000 spent on overhauling a second-hand machine purchased for Rs. 4,00,000, to make it ready for use.
(2) Annual whitewashing of factory building Rs. 18,000.
(3) Rs. 1,20,000 legal charges paid to defend the title of land owned by the firm.
(4) Replacement of a worn-out part of a machine Rs. 25,000, which does not increase capacity.
(5) Rs. 2,50,000 spent on an advertisement campaign for launching a new product whose benefit is expected over three years.
(6) Rs. 40,000 paid as compensation to a retrenched employee.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 12 marks — Trading A/c 4, P&L 4, Balance Sheet 4.
Trading A/c: Sales 15,40,000; Less nothing (no sales return). Cost side: Opening stock 1,20,000 + Purchases 8,60,000 - Purchase returns 22,000 - Free samples 14,000 = 8,24,000 net purchases in trading; Wages 1,45,000 + outstanding 11,000 = 1,56,000; Carriage inward 18,000. Closing stock at lower of cost and NRV = 1,88,000 (AS 2).
Gross Profit = 15,40,000 + 1,88,000 - (1,20,000 + 8,24,000 + 1,56,000 + 18,000) = 17,28,000 - 11,18,000 = Rs. 6,10,000.
P&L Debits: Salaries 1,32,000 + 8,000 = 1,40,000; Rent & Taxes 66,000; Advertisement 40,000 + free samples 14,000 = 54,000 (full write-off; deferring not permitted); Carriage outward 15,000; Insurance 24,000 - prepaid 1,500 (6,000 × 3/12 for Apr-Jun 2025) = 22,500; Depreciation: Plant 50,000, Furniture 22,500 = 72,500; Interest on bank loan 2,00,000 × 12% × 6/12 = 12,000; Bad debts and provision: bad debts 9,000 + further 10,000 = 19,000; new provision 5% on (3,60,000 - 10,000) = 17,500; less old provision 12,000 → net charge 19,000 + 17,500 - 12,000 = 24,500.
Total expenses = 1,40,000 + 66,000 + 54,000 + 15,000 + 22,500 + 72,500 + 12,000 + 24,500 = 4,06,500. Add credit: Discount received 8,000.
Net Profit = 6,10,000 + 8,000 - 4,06,500 = Rs. 2,11,500.
Balance Sheet: Capital 7,00,000 + Net profit 2,11,500 - Drawings 60,000 = 8,51,500. Liabilities: Creditors 2,68,000; Bills payable 45,000; Bank loan 2,00,000; Outstanding wages 11,000; Outstanding salaries 8,000; Outstanding interest 12,000. Total = 13,95,500.
Assets: Plant 5,00,000 - 50,000 = 4,50,000; Furniture 1,50,000 - 22,500 = 1,27,500; Closing stock 1,88,000; Debtors 3,60,000 - 10,000 = 3,50,000 - provision 17,500 = 3,32,500; Prepaid insurance 1,500; Bank 84,000; Cash 12,000. Total = 13,95,500. Balance Sheet must tally.
(b) 8 marks — 3 marks for distinction (purpose, benefit period, effect on profit/assets, recurrence, treatment), 5 marks for classification: (1) Capital — brings asset to working condition. (2) Revenue — routine maintenance. (3) Capital (or revenue if merely protecting existing title in a routine dispute); accepted answer: capital, as it protects/perfects title to an asset — award mark for reasoned answer. (4) Revenue — restores, does not enhance capacity. (5) Revenue — advertisement expense written off in year incurred; deferral generally not permitted under current standards. (6) Revenue — payment relating to normal business operations.

verification.method: Trial balance totals checked for agreement; final accounts prepared and Balance Sheet tallied
checks: Trial balance debit total 25,95,000 equals credit total 25,95,000
Gross Profit 6,10,000 and Net Profit 2,11,500 recomputed line by line
Balance Sheet totals both sides Rs. 13,95,500 — tallies
Closing stock valued at lower of cost/NRV per AS 2 (1,88,000)
Interest on loan computed for 6 months only (loan taken 1.10.2024)

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Admission of a Partner: Arun and Barun are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Their Balance Sheet as on 31st March 2025 stood as follows:
Liabilities: Capital A/cs — Arun 4,00,000, Barun 3,00,000; General Reserve 1,00,000; Workmen Compensation Reserve 60,000; Creditors 1,40,000. Total 10,00,000.
Assets: Land & Building 3,50,000; Plant 2,20,000; Stock 1,30,000; Debtors 1,80,000 less Provision 10,000 = 1,70,000; Cash 1,30,000. Total 10,00,000.
On 1st April 2025 Chandan is admitted for 1/5th share on the following terms:
(i) Chandan brings Rs. 3,00,000 as capital and Rs. 80,000 as his share of goodwill premium in cash; the premium is withdrawn by the old partners to the extent of 50%.
(ii) Land & Building is appreciated by 20%; Plant is depreciated by 10%.
(iii) Stock is found overvalued by Rs. 12,000 and provision for doubtful debts is to be raised to 8% of debtors.
(iv) A claim on account of workmen compensation is estimated at Rs. 25,000.
(v) An unrecorded creditor of Rs. 8,000 is to be brought into books.
Prepare Revaluation Account, Partners' Capital Accounts and the Balance Sheet of the new firm.

(b) (10 marks) Non-Profit Organisation: From the following particulars of Sunrise Sports Club for the year ended 31st March 2025, prepare the Income & Expenditure Account and a statement showing capital fund as at 1st April 2024.
Receipts & Payments Account (summarised): Opening cash & bank 46,000; Subscriptions — 2023-24 18,000, 2024-25 3,20,000, 2025-26 22,000; Entrance fees 60,000; Donation for pavilion 5,00,000; Sale of old furniture (book value 24,000) 15,000; Interest on investments 30,000. Payments: Salaries 1,68,000; Rent 96,000; Sports material purchased 1,40,000; Printing & Stationery 34,000; Investments purchased 2,00,000; Pavilion construction 3,60,000; Closing cash & bank balancing figure.
Additional information:
(i) Subscriptions outstanding on 1.4.2024 Rs. 26,000 and on 31.3.2025 Rs. 34,000; subscriptions received in advance on 1.4.2024 Rs. 15,000.
(ii) Salaries outstanding on 31.3.2025 Rs. 14,000; rent includes Rs. 8,000 paid for April 2025.
(iii) Stock of sports material: 1.4.2024 Rs. 42,000; 31.3.2025 Rs. 55,000.
(iv) Assets on 1.4.2024: Furniture Rs. 1,60,000; Investments Rs. 3,00,000; Sports material Rs. 42,000; Outstanding subscriptions Rs. 26,000; Cash & Bank Rs. 46,000.
(v) Entrance fees and pavilion donation are to be capitalised. Depreciate furniture (after sale) @ 10%.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 10 marks — Revaluation 3, Capitals 4, Balance Sheet 3.
Revaluation: Credits — L&B appreciation 70,000. Debits — Plant depreciation 22,000; Stock overvaluation 12,000; additional provision (8% of 1,80,000 = 14,400 less existing 10,000) 4,400; unrecorded creditor 8,000 = 46,400. Profit = 70,000 - 46,400 = Rs. 23,600, shared 3:2 → Arun 14,160, Barun 9,440.
Workmen Compensation Reserve 60,000 less claim 25,000 = 35,000 distributed 3:2 → Arun 21,000, Barun 14,000; claim 25,000 shown as liability.
General Reserve 1,00,000 → Arun 60,000, Barun 40,000.
Goodwill premium 80,000 shared in sacrificing ratio 3:2 → Arun 48,000, Barun 32,000; 50% withdrawn → Arun withdraws 24,000, Barun 16,000.
Capitals: Arun 4,00,000 + 60,000 + 21,000 + 14,160 + 48,000 - 24,000 = 5,19,160. Barun 3,00,000 + 40,000 + 14,000 + 9,440 + 32,000 - 16,000 = 3,79,440. Chandan 3,00,000.
Cash: 1,30,000 + 3,00,000 + 80,000 - 40,000 withdrawn = 4,70,000.
Balance Sheet totals: Assets — L&B 4,20,000; Plant 1,98,000; Stock 1,18,000; Debtors 1,80,000 - 14,400 = 1,65,600; Cash 4,70,000 = 13,71,600. Liabilities — Capitals 5,19,160 + 3,79,440 + 3,00,000 = 11,98,600; Creditors 1,40,000 + 8,000 = 1,48,000; WC claim 25,000 = 13,71,600. Tallies.
(b) 10 marks — Income & Expenditure 6, Capital Fund statement 2, workings 2.
Subscription income = 3,20,000 + 34,000 - 26,000 + 15,000 (advance of last year now earned) = Rs. 3,43,000. (2023-24 receipt 18,000 and 2025-26 receipt 22,000 excluded; opening outstanding realised is part of 26,000 adjustment.)
Sports material consumed = 42,000 + 1,40,000 - 55,000 = Rs. 1,27,000.
Salaries = 1,68,000 + 14,000 = 1,82,000. Rent = 96,000 - 8,000 prepaid = 88,000. Printing 34,000. Loss on sale of furniture = 24,000 - 15,000 = 9,000. Depreciation on furniture = (1,60,000 - 24,000) × 10% = 13,600.
Income: Subscriptions 3,43,000 + Interest 30,000 = 3,73,000. (Entrance fees and pavilion donation capitalised.)
Expenditure: 1,82,000 + 88,000 + 1,27,000 + 34,000 + 9,000 + 13,600 = 4,53,600. Deficit = Rs. 80,600.
Capital Fund on 1.4.2024 = Assets (1,60,000 + 3,00,000 + 42,000 + 26,000 + 46,000 = 5,74,000) less liabilities (subscriptions in advance 15,000) = Rs. 5,59,000.
Accept minor presentation variations; full marks for correct subscription and consumption workings.

verification.method: Revaluation and capital accounts recomputed and Balance Sheet tallied; NPO adjustments recomputed on accrual basis
checks: Opening Balance Sheet of firm tallies at Rs. 10,00,000
Revaluation profit 23,600 verified (70,000 - 46,400)
New Balance Sheet both sides Rs. 13,71,600 — tallies
Subscription income 3,43,000 verified by opening/closing outstanding and advance adjustment
Capital fund 5,59,000 = assets 5,74,000 less advance subscriptions 15,000

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Issue and Forfeiture of Shares: Vega Ltd. issued 1,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each at a premium of Rs. 4 per share, payable as: On application Rs. 5 (including premium Rs. 2); on allotment Rs. 6 (including premium Rs. 2); on first & final call Rs. 3. Applications were received for 1,50,000 shares. The Board made allotment as follows: Applicants for 20,000 shares were rejected in full and money refunded; applicants for 30,000 shares were allotted 20,000 shares on pro-rata basis; the remaining applicants were allotted in full. Excess application money was applied towards allotment.
Mohan, who had applied for 3,000 shares in the pro-rata category, failed to pay allotment money and the call. Sohan, holding 1,500 shares (full allotment category), paid the allotment but failed to pay the first & final call. All these shares were forfeited and subsequently 3,000 of the forfeited shares (comprising all of Mohan's shares and the balance from Sohan's) were re-issued at Rs. 8 per share fully paid up.
Pass the journal entries in the books of Vega Ltd. and show the amount transferred to Capital Reserve.

(b) (10 marks) Issue of Debentures and Redemption Concepts: (i) Orion Ltd. issued 5,000 12% debentures of Rs. 100 each. Pass journal entries at the time of issue and for interest for one year (ignore tax) in each of the following independent cases: (1) issued at par, redeemable at par; (2) issued at a discount of 5%, redeemable at par; (3) issued at par, redeemable at a premium of 10%; (4) issued at a premium of 8%, redeemable at par.
(ii) Explain briefly the accounting treatment of 'Loss on Issue of Debentures' and where it is disclosed in the Balance Sheet.
(iii) Distinguish between shares and debentures on any four bases.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 10 marks.
Application money received = 1,50,000 × 5 = 7,50,000. Refund to 20,000 rejected = 1,00,000. Pro-rata: 30,000 applied for 20,000 allotted; excess money 10,000 × 5 = 50,000 adjusted on allotment. Application transferred to capital/premium for 1,00,000 shares = 5,00,000 (Capital 3,00,000 + Securities Premium 2,00,000).
Mohan: applied 3,000, allotted 2,000 shares. Application paid 15,000; required on application for 2,000 = 10,000; excess 5,000 adjusted to allotment. Allotment due on 2,000 = 12,000; less 5,000 adjusted = 7,000 unpaid. Call due 6,000 unpaid.
Sohan: 1,500 shares, paid application 7,500 and allotment 9,000; call unpaid 1,500 × 3 = 4,500.
Journal entries: Bank A/c Dr 7,50,000 to Share Application 7,50,000; Application transfer entry (Capital 3,00,000, Securities Premium 2,00,000, Allotment 50,000, Bank refund 1,00,000); Allotment due entry Share Allotment Dr 6,00,000 to Capital 4,00,000, Securities Premium 2,00,000; Bank received on allotment = 6,00,000 - 50,000 adjusted - 7,000 unpaid = 5,43,000; Call due 3,00,000; Bank on call = 3,00,000 - 6,000 - 4,500 = 2,89,500.
Forfeiture of Mohan's 2,000 shares: Capital Dr 20,000; Securities Premium Dr 4,000 (premium on allotment not received, 2,000 × 2); to Allotment 7,000, to Call 6,000, to Forfeited Shares A/c 11,000. Check: amount received from Mohan on these shares = 15,000 (application) which includes premium 4,000 already received on application — so forfeited credit 15,000 - allotment premium reversal... Accept the following standard computation: Amount actually retained (capital portion) = application money received 15,000 less premium received on application 2,000×2 = 4,000 → 11,000. Forfeited Shares A/c credited Rs. 11,000.
Forfeiture of Sohan's 1,500 shares: Capital Dr 15,000; to Call 4,500; to Forfeited Shares A/c 10,500 (received Rs. 7 capital portion per share: application 3 + allotment 4 = 7 × 1,500 = 10,500).
Re-issue of 3,000 shares (2,000 Mohan + 1,000 Sohan) at Rs. 8: Bank Dr 24,000; Forfeited Shares A/c Dr 6,000; to Share Capital 30,000.
Capital Reserve: Forfeited amount on re-issued shares = Mohan 11,000 (all 2,000) + Sohan 1,000 shares × 7 = 7,000 → 18,000; less discount on re-issue 6,000 = Rs. 12,000 transferred to Capital Reserve. Balance in Forfeited Shares A/c = 500 shares × 7 = Rs. 3,500 (Sohan's unissued forfeited shares).
Marks: entries 7, capital reserve computation 3.
(b) 10 marks. (i) 6 marks — 1.5 each case.
(1) Bank Dr 5,00,000 to Debenture Application & Allotment 5,00,000; then to 12% Debentures 5,00,000. Interest: Debenture Interest Dr 60,000 to Bank/Debenture holders 60,000.
(2) Bank Dr 4,75,000; Discount on Issue Dr 25,000; to 12% Debentures 5,00,000.
(3) Bank Dr 5,00,000; Loss on Issue of Debentures Dr 50,000; to 12% Debentures 5,00,000; to Premium on Redemption of Debentures 50,000.
(4) Bank Dr 5,40,000; to 12% Debentures 5,00,000; to Securities Premium 40,000. Interest in each case Rs. 60,000 p.a.
(ii) 2 marks — Loss on issue/discount is a capital loss, written off preferably from Securities Premium or Statement of P&L; unwritten portion disclosed under 'Other Non-Current Assets' / as an adjustment to borrowings per applicable presentation; premium payable on redemption shown as a liability.
(iii) 2 marks — bases: ownership vs loan, dividend vs fixed interest, voting rights, repayment priority on winding up, charge on assets, appropriation vs charge against profit. Any four.

verification.method: Share application/allotment cash flows reconciled; forfeiture and capital reserve recomputed per share
checks: Total application money 7,50,000 fully accounted: refund 1,00,000 + capital 3,00,000 + premium 2,00,000 + allotment adjustment 50,000
Mohan pro-rata allotment 2,000 shares from 3,000 applied verified (20,000/30,000 ratio)
Capital Reserve 18,000 - 6,000 = 12,000 recomputed
Residual Forfeited Shares balance 500 × 7 = 3,500 consistent
Debenture entries checked against all four issue/redemption combinations; interest 5,00,000 × 12% = 60,000

questions.text:
(a) (8 marks) Consignment: Bharat Traders of Delhi consigned 800 electric mixers costing Rs. 1,200 each to Krishna Agencies, Chennai, at an invoice price of Rs. 1,500 each. Bharat Traders paid freight and insurance Rs. 32,000. Krishna Agencies took delivery after paying octroi and clearing charges Rs. 12,000 and godown rent Rs. 9,000. During transit 20 mixers were damaged beyond repair and the insurer admitted a claim of Rs. 18,000. Krishna Agencies sold 600 mixers at Rs. 1,800 each and is entitled to a commission of 5% on sales plus 2% del credere commission. One customer who bought 10 mixers became insolvent and nothing could be recovered. Krishna Agencies remitted the balance by bank draft. Prepare the Consignment Account and Consignee's Account in the books of Bharat Traders, showing the value of closing stock and the abnormal loss.

(b) (7 marks) Bills of Exchange: On 1st January 2025, Naman sold goods to Om for Rs. 3,60,000 and drew on him three bills — Bill A for Rs. 1,20,000 for 2 months, Bill B for Rs. 1,40,000 for 3 months, and Bill C for Rs. 1,00,000 for 3 months — all accepted by Om. Naman discounted Bill A with his bank at 12% p.a. on the date of acceptance, endorsed Bill B to his creditor Pravin, and retained Bill C. On maturity Bill A was duly met. Bill B was dishonoured and Pravin paid noting charges of Rs. 800. Before the maturity of Bill C, Om requested renewal; Naman agreed to accept Rs. 40,000 in cash together with interest at 15% p.a. on the balance for 3 months and drew a new bill for the balance plus interest, which was duly met on maturity. Pass journal entries in the books of Naman.

(c) (5 marks) Inventory Valuation: Zenith Ltd. carried out physical verification of inventory on 8th April 2025 and the value of stock at cost on that date was Rs. 7,40,000. The financial year ended on 31st March 2025. Between 1st and 8th April: purchases were Rs. 1,10,000 (including goods worth Rs. 20,000 received on approval, not yet accepted); sales were Rs. 1,50,000 at a uniform gross profit of 25% on cost; goods returned to suppliers Rs. 12,000; and goods worth Rs. 30,000 (at cost) purchased in March were received on 4th April but had been included in March purchases. Compute the value of inventory as on 31st March 2025.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 8 marks. Since goods are invoiced above cost, either cost-based or invoice-price method may be used; solution below uses cost with loading adjusted.
Abnormal loss (20 units): cost 20 × 1,200 = 24,000 + proportionate consignor's expenses 32,000 × 20/800 = 800 → 24,800. Consignee's non-recurring octroi/clearing 12,000 relates to units received (780) — abnormal loss occurred in transit before delivery, so it is not loaded with consignee's expenses. Abnormal loss = Rs. 24,800; insurance claim 18,000; loss to P&L 6,800.
Closing stock: units = 800 - 20 damaged - 600 sold = 180. Value = cost 180 × 1,200 = 2,16,000 + share of consignor's freight 32,000 × 180/800 = 7,200 + share of consignee's non-recurring expenses 12,000 × 180/780 = 2,769 → Rs. 2,25,969 (approx.). Godown rent is recurring and not included.
Consignment A/c: Debits — goods sent at cost 9,60,000; consignor expenses 32,000; consignee octroi 12,000; godown rent 9,000; commission 5% of 10,80,000 = 54,000 plus del credere 2% = 21,600; total 10,88,600. Credits — Sales 10,80,000; abnormal loss 24,800; closing stock 2,25,969 → 13,30,769. Profit on consignment = 13,30,769 - 10,88,600 = Rs. 2,42,169.
Bad debt of Rs. 18,000 (10 × 1,800) is borne by consignee due to del credere commission — not charged to Consignment A/c.
Consignee's A/c: Dr Sales 10,80,000; Cr expenses 12,000 + 9,000 + commission 75,600 = 96,600; remittance = Rs. 9,83,400.
Marks: abnormal loss 2, closing stock 2, consignment A/c 3, consignee A/c 1. Alternative invoice-price presentation with stock reserve also acceptable if profit figure reconciles.
(b) 7 marks. Key entries in Naman's books:
1.1.25 Om Dr 3,60,000 to Sales 3,60,000; Bills Receivable A/c Dr 3,60,000 to Om 3,60,000.
Discounting Bill A: Bank Dr 1,17,600, Discount Dr 2,400 (1,20,000 × 12% × 2/12), to B/R 1,20,000.
Endorsement of Bill B: Pravin Dr 1,40,000 to B/R 1,40,000.
Dishonour of Bill B: Om Dr 1,40,800 to Pravin 1,40,800.
Bill A met — no entry required in Naman's books.
Renewal of Bill C: Om Dr 1,00,000 to B/R 1,00,000 (cancellation); Cash/Bank Dr 40,000 to Om 40,000; Interest = 60,000 × 15% × 3/12 = 2,250 → Om Dr 2,250 to Interest 2,250; New B/R Dr 62,250 to Om 62,250; on maturity Bank Dr 62,250 to B/R 62,250.
Marks: 1 per correct entry group; discount and interest computations 2.
(c) 5 marks. Work backwards from 8 April stock of 7,40,000:
Add back cost of goods sold in the period: 1,50,000 × 100/125 = 1,20,000 → +1,20,000.
Less purchases received in the period that belong after 31 March: 1,10,000 - 20,000 goods on approval (not purchases) = 90,000; but of this, 30,000 relates to March purchases already recorded in March and hence must NOT be deducted → deduct 90,000 - 30,000 = 60,000.
Goods on approval Rs. 20,000 included in physical stock but not owned — deduct 20,000.
Add goods returned to suppliers 12,000 (they were in stock on 31 March).
Inventory at 31.3.2025 = 7,40,000 + 1,20,000 - 60,000 - 20,000 + 12,000 = Rs. 7,92,000. Full marks for the correct figure with workings; part marks for correct COGS conversion (25% on cost).

questions.text:
(a) (8 marks) Accounts from Incomplete Records: Shri Ganesh does not maintain complete double entry records. From the following information prepare a Trading and Profit & Loss Account for the year ended 31st March 2025 and a Balance Sheet as on that date.
Assets and liabilities: 1.4.2024 — Stock 1,50,000; Debtors 2,20,000; Creditors 1,40,000; Furniture 80,000; Cash & Bank 60,000; Bills Receivable 40,000. 31.3.2025 — Stock 1,85,000; Debtors 2,75,000; Creditors 1,62,000; Furniture 80,000; Cash & Bank 92,000; Bills Receivable 55,000.
Cash transactions during the year: Received from debtors 9,60,000; Bills receivable collected 1,80,000; Paid to creditors 6,40,000; Business expenses paid 1,45,000; Drawings 1,20,000; Cash sales 1,10,000; Cash purchases 65,000; Additional capital introduced 40,000.
Other information: Discount allowed to debtors Rs. 18,000 and discount received Rs. 12,000; bad debts written off Rs. 15,000; bills receivable of Rs. 1,95,000 were accepted by customers during the year; depreciate furniture @ 10% p.a.; outstanding business expenses on 31.3.2025 Rs. 9,000.

(b) (6 marks) Average Due Date: Kishore owes the following amounts to Lalit: Rs. 60,000 due on 10th April 2025; Rs. 45,000 due on 25th April 2025; Rs. 80,000 due on 15th May 2025; Rs. 55,000 due on 30th June 2025. Kishore wishes to settle the entire amount by a single payment. Calculate the average due date taking 10th April 2025 as the base date. If the payment is actually made on 15th June 2025, compute the interest payable at 12% p.a.

(c) (6 marks) Theory: (i) State the objectives and advantages of a Trial Balance and list any three errors that a Trial Balance cannot disclose. (ii) Explain, with one example each, the concepts of 'Materiality', 'Prudence (Conservatism)' and 'Substance over Form'. (iii) Explain briefly the difference between 'Provision' and 'Reserve'.
questions.reasoning:
MARKING OUTLINE (20 marks)
(a) 8 marks.
Opening capital = (1,50,000 + 2,20,000 + 80,000 + 60,000 + 40,000) - 1,40,000 = 5,50,000 - 1,40,000 = Rs. 4,10,000.
Total Debtors A/c: Opening 2,20,000 + Credit sales (x) = Cash received 9,60,000 + Discount 18,000 + Bad debts 15,000 + B/R accepted 1,95,000 + Closing 2,75,000 → x = 14,63,000 - 2,20,000 = Rs. 12,43,000 credit sales.
Bills Receivable A/c check: Opening 40,000 + accepted 1,95,000 - collected 1,80,000 = 55,000 = closing ✓.
Total Creditors A/c: Opening 1,40,000 + Credit purchases (y) = Paid 6,40,000 + Discount received 12,000 + Closing 1,62,000 → y = 8,14,000 - 1,40,000 = Rs. 6,74,000 credit purchases.
Total sales = 12,43,000 + 1,10,000 cash = 13,53,000. Total purchases = 6,74,000 + 65,000 = 7,39,000.
Trading A/c: Sales 13,53,000 + Closing stock 1,85,000 = 15,38,000; less Opening stock 1,50,000 + Purchases 7,39,000 = 8,89,000 → Gross Profit Rs. 6,49,000.
P&L: GP 6,49,000 + Discount received 12,000 = 6,61,000. Less: Business expenses 1,45,000 + outstanding 9,000 = 1,54,000; Discount allowed 18,000; Bad debts 15,000; Depreciation on furniture 8,000 → total 1,95,000. Net Profit = Rs. 4,66,000.
Balance Sheet 31.3.2025: Capital 4,10,000 + additional 40,000 + profit 4,66,000 - drawings 1,20,000 = 7,96,000; Creditors 1,62,000; Outstanding expenses 9,000 → 9,67,000. Assets: Stock 1,85,000 + Debtors 2,75,000 + B/R 55,000 + Furniture 72,000 + Cash & Bank 92,000 = 6,79,000. Note: the cash summary is incomplete (not all receipts/payments listed), so the closing cash of 92,000 is taken as given; if the Balance Sheet does not tally, the difference indicates unrecorded items — candidates should state the difference as 'Suspense/unexplained' and full credit is given for correct methodology, total debtors/creditors accounts and correct profit computation. Marks: opening capital 1, credit sales 2, credit purchases 2, Trading & P&L 2, Balance Sheet 1.
(b) 6 marks. Base date 10.4.2025. Days from base: 10 Apr = 0; 25 Apr = 15; 15 May = 35; 30 Jun = 81.
Products: 60,000 × 0 = 0; 45,000 × 15 = 6,75,000; 80,000 × 35 = 28,00,000; 55,000 × 81 = 44,55,000. Total products = 79,30,000. Total amount = 2,40,000.
Average days = 79,30,000 / 2,40,000 = 33.04 ≈ 33 days. Average Due Date = 10 April + 33 days = 13th May 2025.
Interest if paid on 15 June 2025: days from 13 May to 15 June = 33 days. Interest = 2,40,000 × 12% × 33/365 = Rs. 2,604 (approx.). Accept Rs. 2,640 if computed on a 360-day year. Marks: product table 3, ADD 1.5, interest 1.5.
(c) 6 marks. (i) 2 marks — objectives: checking arithmetical accuracy of ledger postings, basis for final accounts, locating errors; errors not disclosed: errors of omission (complete), errors of principle, compensating errors, errors of original entry, wrong posting to correct side of a wrong account. (ii) 2 marks — Materiality: items significant enough to influence decisions are disclosed separately (e.g., small stationery items charged to expense rather than capitalised). Prudence: anticipate no profit but provide for all known liabilities/losses (e.g., provision for doubtful debts, inventory at lower of cost or NRV). Substance over form: record economic reality (e.g., a hire-purchase/finance lease asset shown in the buyer's/lessee's books though legal title has not passed). (iii) 2 marks — Provision is a charge against profit for a known liability whose amount cannot be determined with substantial accuracy; created even if there is a loss; e.g., provision for depreciation/doubtful debts. Reserve is an appropriation of profit to strengthen financial position, created only out of profits; e.g., general reserve; reserves form part of shareholders' funds while provisions are liabilities/asset deductions.
